subject.title: [Feature] Allow configuring Gemini safety settings in OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw expose operator-controlled Gemini safety thresholds as a supported Google-provider configuration contract, or retain Gemini’s upstream defaults?
rationale: The feature adds a durable provider configuration surface that can relax content filtering; code can implement either outcome, but only maintainers can choose the intended safety and compatibility policy.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow Google-provider contract
options.body: Define supported Gemini categories and thresholds, scope them to the Google Generative AI adapter, document precedence, and require focused configuration and payload tests.

options.title: Retain upstream safety defaults
options.body: Decline a configurable override and document that OpenClaw does not alter Gemini safety filtering.

options.title: Request a narrower proposal
options.body: Ask for a proposal limited to documented Google API values and a single provider-owned configuration shape before deciding whether to add it.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow Google-provider contract
recommendation.body: Define supported Gemini categories and thresholds, scope them to the Google Generative AI adapter, document precedence, and require focused configuration and payload tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously reviewed this exact request and are the strongest available routing signal for the affected Google/configuration paths.
